stories.headline: Italy marks 81st Liberation Day amid street violence, political tensions, and Israeli Brigade controversy
stories.summary: Italy's April 25 Liberation Day celebrations were marked by multiple incidents: two ANPI members were shot with an air pistol at Rome's Parco Schuster, pro-Palestinian activists blocked the Jewish Brigade from marching in Milan and directed antisemitic slurs, Bologna protesters threw vegetables at an FdI party office, and FdI offices in Pescara were vandalized. Mattarella delivered a speech in San Severino Marche repeating his 'Ora e sempre Resistenza' motto and implicitly rebuking Senate President La Russa's equivalence between partisans and Salò fighters. Meloni attended the Altare della Patria ceremony and called the day a 'moment of national cohesion.' Tajani represented the government at the Fosse Ardeatine. Salvini attended the American Cemetery at Tavarnuzze, avoiding ANPI-organised marches.

stories.headline: Russian TV host Solovyev hurls personal insults at Meloni; Italy summons Russian ambassador
stories.summary: Pro-Kremlin TV anchor Vladimir Solovyev attacked Prime Minister Meloni with vulgar personal insults in Italian during his prime-time programme, calling her a 'certified idiot' and worse while accusing her of betraying Trump and supporting Ukraine. Italy's Foreign Minister Tajani summoned the Russian ambassador in protest; Mattarella sent Meloni a solidarity message; Crosetto condemned the attack; and Solovyev subsequently targeted Mattarella as well. The incident was attributed to Meloni's recent meeting with Zelensky and Italy's continued support for Ukraine.

stories.headline: Security decree approved with emergency correction after Mattarella pressure; parliament erupts over 'Bella Ciao' vs national anthem
stories.summary: The government's Decreto Sicurezza passed the Chamber on April 24 after a contentious process: President Mattarella had informally objected to Article 30-bis (a bonus payment for lawyers who secure voluntary deportations), prompting the government to pass an immediate corrective decree in parallel. Mattarella signed both, but Il Manifesto reported he did so silently without an explanatory note. The parliamentary session saw PD members sing 'Bella Ciao', to which FdI responded with the national anthem, while Salvini dismissed the exchange. Meloni defended the original norm as 'common sense.'

stories.headline: Meloni at Cyprus EU informal summit presses for energy carve-out from stability rules amid Iran crisis
stories.summary: Prime Minister Meloni attended the informal EU summit in Cyprus (Nicosia) and called on the EU to allow defence and energy spending to be excluded from deficit calculations under the Stability Pact, citing the Iran war as an acute energy emergency. The European Commission and Germany resisted, with Commission VP Dombrovskis saying there was no case for suspending the Pact. Meloni also stated Italy's relationship with the US remained solid but declined to say she had spoken with Trump, and said it was not Italy's moment to make gestures toward Putin regarding a G20 invitation.

stories.headline: Italian leaders express solidarity with Trump after shooting at White House Correspondents' Dinner
stories.summary: Following shots fired at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington, Meloni was among the first foreign leaders to post solidarity, writing 'no space for political hatred in our democracies.' Tajani echoed the message on the need to calm political debate. Salvini called it an 'alarming signal.' La Russa condemned it as well. The incident drew broad cross-party statements from Italian politicians.

stories.headline: Switzerland demands Italy reimburse medical costs for Crans-Montana fire victims; Meloni calls the request 'ignoble'
stories.summary: Switzerland's social insurance office said it would bill Italy over 100,000 Swiss francs for treating four Italian nationals at a Sion hospital after the Crans-Montana New Year's Eve fire that killed 41. Meloni called the request 'ignoble' and said Italy would reject it; Tajani said 'it is obvious we will not pay'; and the Italian ambassador to Switzerland indicated Rome considered the matter closed. A family of one victim said they had separately received a bill for 68,000 francs.
